---
title: "Notebooks"
---

Hands-on **PyTorch** notebooks — each grows out of a lecture. Every one is sized in *hours, not days*; most run on a free Colab GPU and several need no GPU at all. Download to run locally, or open in Colab. These are also the seeds of the [homeworks](labs/index.qmd) — each assignment takes one you've already run and pushes it further.

The **spine** and **landscape** notebooks below are the large, project-style builds. Separately, every one of the first thirteen lectures ships one or two **minimal per-lecture notebooks** — tiny (≈5–12 cells, numpy/torch only), each isolating a single idea and reproducing the exact numbers worked on the slides. Jump to those in the [per-lecture minimal notebooks](#per-lecture-minimal-notebooks) table.

## Primer · Probability & MLE

| Notebook | Lecture | What you do |
|---|:---:|---|
| [iid-demo](notebooks/lec00-iid-demo.ipynb) | L00 | IID vs non-IID — sequences, histograms, lag-1 scatter; why `sum(log p)` is blind to autocorrelation |
| [bernoulli-playground](notebooks/lec00-bernoulli-playground.ipynb) | L00 | The three operations on a Bernoulli — sample, PMF, log-prob — and MLE by hand |
| [mle-map](notebooks/lec00-mle-map.ipynb) | L00B | MLE → MAP in PyTorch: ridge and lasso emerge from Gaussian / Laplace priors |

## Per-lecture minimal notebooks

One or two per lecture for the first thirteen. Each is deliberately tiny — a single idea, seeds fixed, numpy/torch/matplotlib only — and reproduces the numbers worked on that lecture's slides. Ideal for a five-minute in-class run or a quick self-check.

|:---:|---|---|---|
| 1 | Why These Losses? | [gaussian-nll-is-mse](notebooks/L01/01_gaussian_nll_is_mse.ipynb) | Gaussian negative log-likelihood **is** MSE (up to a constant) |
| 1 | | [softmax-cross-entropy](notebooks/L01/02_softmax_cross_entropy.ipynb) | softmax → cross-entropy; the gradient is exactly `p − y` (vs finite differences) |
| 2 | Linear → MLP | [linear-regression-gd](notebooks/L02/01_linear_regression_gd.ipynb) | fit a line by gradient descent from scratch |
| 2 | | [mlp-xor](notebooks/L02/02_mlp_xor.ipynb) | a 2-layer MLP cracks XOR that no linear model can |
| 3 | Calculus Toolkit | [gradient-descent-on-quadratics](notebooks/L03A/03_gradient_descent_on_quadratics.ipynb) | curvature & step size on a quadratic bowl |
| 3 | | [jacobian-vjp-hessian](notebooks/L03A/05_jacobian_vjp_hessian_pytorch.ipynb) | Jacobian, VJP and Hessian via PyTorch autograd |
| 4 | Backpropagation | [manual-scalar-backprop](notebooks/L03/01_manual_scalar_backprop.ipynb) | backprop through `(wx+b−y)²` by hand: `∇w=−18, ∇b=−6` |
| 4 | | [autograd-scalar](notebooks/L03/02_autograd_scalar.ipynb) | the same with autograd, and how `.grad` accumulates |
| 5 | Optimization | [gd-quadratic](notebooks/L05/01_gd_quadratic.ipynb) | GD trace on `(θ−3)²`: `0.6, 1.08, 1.464, …` |
